blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 1 (Complex Numbers), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Show that every non-zero complex number \((a, b)\) has the multiplicative inverse \(\left(\dfrac{a}{a^{2}+b^{2}}, \dfrac{-b}{a^{2}+b^{2}}\right)\). Hence find the multiplicative inverse of \((2, 5)\) and verify it. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write \((a, b)\) as \(a + ib\), divide 1 by it using the conjugate, then apply to \((2, 5)\).

book_ref.quote: Every non-zero complex number (i.e. a number not equal to

steps: \(\dfrac{1}{a + ib} = \dfrac{a - ib}{(a + ib)(a - ib)} = \dfrac{a - ib}{a^{2} + b^{2}}\), i.e. the pair \(\left(\dfrac{a}{a^{2}+b^{2}}, \dfrac{-b}{a^{2}+b^{2}}\right)\)

blocks.prompt: 2 For \(z_1 = 3 + 2i\) and \(z_2 = -1 + 4i\), verify that (i) \(\overline{z_1 + z_2} = \overline{z_1} + \overline{z_2}\) (ii) \(\overline{\left(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\right)} = \dfrac{\overline{z_1}}{\overline{z_2}}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Work out each side separately; divide using the conjugate of the denominator.

book_ref.quote: always multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator

blocks.prompt: 3 If \(z_1 = 2 - 3i\) and \(z_2 = 1 + 4i\), find \(z_1 z_2\) and \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\) in the form \(x + iy\), and verify that \(|z_1 z_2| = |z_1||z_2|\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Multiply out; divide with the conjugate; then compare the two moduli.

book_ref.quote: the modulus of a complex number is the distance from the origin

blocks.prompt: 4 Find real \(x\) and \(y\) if \((x + iy)(2 - 3i) = 4 + i\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expand the left side, compare real and imaginary parts, and solve the two equations by elimination.

book_ref.quote: One complex equation gives two real equations

blocks.prompt: 5 Find real \(x\) and \(y\) if \((x + 2i)(1 - i) + y(2 + i) = 9 + i\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Bring the left side to the form (real part) + (imaginary part)\(i\), then compare.

book_ref.quote: this rule lets us find two unknowns

blocks.prompt: 6 Derive the formula for the square roots of the complex number \(z = x + iy\). (5 marks)

book_ref.quote: Equation (v) is the required formula for the square root of complex numbers.

steps: Let \(w = p + iq\) (\(p, q\) real) with \(w^{2} = z\): \(p^{2} - q^{2} + 2pqi = x + iy\)
Adding and subtracting (ii) and (iv): \(2p^{2} = |z| + x\), \(2q^{2} = |z| - x\), so \(p = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{|z| + x}{2}}\), \(q = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{|z| - x}{2}}\)
By (iii), \(p, q\) have the same sign if \(y > 0\) and opposite signs if \(y < 0\); this is the factor \(\dfrac{iy}{|y|}\)

blocks.prompt: 7 Find the square roots of \(-15 + 8i\) and represent them on an Argand diagram. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use formula (v) with \(x = -15\), \(y = 8\); then plot both roots.

book_ref.quote: The two square roots are always opposite each other through the origin

steps: On the Argand diagram: \(1 + 4i\) at \((1, 4)\) (first quadrant), \(-1 - 4i\) at \((-1, -4)\) (third quadrant), opposite through \(O\)

blocks.prompt: 8 Find real \(x\) and \(y\) such that \((x + iy)^{2} = 5 - 12i\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Equate parts to get \(x^{2} - y^{2}\) and \(2xy\); use the modulus for \(x^{2} + y^{2}\).

book_ref.quote: Equating real and imaginary parts, we have

steps: \(xy = -6 < 0\): \(x\) and \(y\) have opposite signs, so \((x, y) = (3, -2)\) or \((-3, 2)\)

blocks.prompt: 9 Factorize \(P(z) = z^{3} - z^{2} + 2\) into linear factors. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find one root with the Rational Root Theorem, divide synthetically, then solve the quadratic.

book_ref.quote: is a mathematical tool used to find all possible rational roots

blocks.prompt: 10 Find the polynomial \(P(z)\) of degree 3 with zeros \(2\), \(1 + 3i\), \(1 - 3i\) and \(P(0) = -40\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write \(P(z) = a(z - z_1)(z - z_2)(z - z_3)\) and fix \(a\) from \(P(0)\).

book_ref.quote: can be factored completely into a constant

blocks.prompt: 11 Find the roots of \(z^{4} + 5z^{2} - 36 = 0\) and hence express \(z^{4} + 5z^{2} - 36\) as a product of linear factors. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Treat it as a quadratic in \(z^{2}\); a degree-4 polynomial has exactly 4 roots.

book_ref.quote: According to the Fundamental theorem of algebra, a polynomial of degree

blocks.prompt: 12 Solve \(3z^{2} + 6z + 15 = 0\) by completing the square and hence write \(3z^{2} + 6z + 15\) as a product of linear factors. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Make the leading coefficient 1, add (half the coefficient of \(z\))\(^{2}\), take square roots, keep the 3 when factorizing.

book_ref.quote: by completing the square we can solve any quadratic equation

blocks.prompt: 13 Solve \(4z^{2} - 12z + 25 = 0\) by completing the square. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Divide by 4, move the constant, add \(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2}\), take square roots.

book_ref.quote: Move the constant term to the right side.

blocks.prompt: 14 Find the three cube roots of unity and prove that (i) each complex root is the square of the other (ii) their sum is zero (iii) their product is 1. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Solve \(x^{3} - 1 = 0\) by factorizing, then check each property by direct calculation.

book_ref.quote: A cube root of unity is a number whose cube is 1.

blocks.final_answer: Roots \(1, \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{3}\,i}{2}, \dfrac{-1 - \sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\); hence proved: \(\omega^{2}\) is the other root, \(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} = 0\), \(\omega^{3} = 1\)

blocks.prompt: 15 Prove that \((1 - \omega + \omega^{2})^{5} + (1 + \omega - \omega^{2})^{5} = 32\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Replace \(1 + \omega^{2}\) by \(-\omega\) and \(1 + \omega\) by \(-\omega^{2}\), then reduce the powers with \(\omega^{3} = 1\).

book_ref.quote: Useful forms: \(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\), \(1 + \omega = -\omega^{2}\)

blocks.prompt: 16 If \(\omega\) is a complex cube root of unity, show that \(\omega^{-1} = \omega^{2}\), and evaluate \(\dfrac{1}{1 + \omega} + \dfrac{1}{1 + \omega^{2}}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(\omega^{3} = 1\) and \(1 + \omega = -\omega^{2}\), \(1 + \omega^{2} = -\omega\).

book_ref.quote: The product of all the three cube roots of unity is unity

blocks.prompt: 17 Find the four fourth roots of unity and prove that (i) their sum is 0 (ii) the real roots are additive inverses of each other (iii) the imaginary roots are conjugates of each other (iv) their product is \(-1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Factor \(x^{4} - 1\) as a difference of two squares, then check each property.

book_ref.quote: A fourth root of unity is a number whose fourth power is 1.

steps: (ii) \(1 + (-1) = 0 = (-1) + 1\): the real roots are additive inverses
blocks.final_answer: Roots \(1, -1, i, -i\); hence proved: sum \(0\), product \(-1\), \(1, -1\) additive inverses, \(i, -i\) conjugates

blocks.prompt: 18 If \(\omega\) is a complex cube root of unity, prove that \(x^{3} + 8 = (x + 2)(x + 2\omega)(x + 2\omega^{2})\) and hence find the three roots of \(x^{3} + 8 = 0\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Start from the R.H.S, multiply the last two brackets, and use \(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\), \(\omega^{3} = 1\).

book_ref.quote: start from the right-hand side (R.H.S), multiply the last two brackets

blocks.prompt: 19 Express \(z = -2\sqrt{3} - 2i\) in polar form using its principal argument, and verify the answer. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find \(r\), decide the quadrant, find the reference angle, then use the table of principal arguments.

book_ref.quote: Find the quadrant first, then use

blocks.prompt: 20 Prove that \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2[\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2) + i\sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2)]\) for \(z_1 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\), \(z_2 = r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\). Hence multiply \(2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\) by \(3\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Open the brackets, use \(i^{2} = -1\), and recognise \(\cos(A + B)\) and \(\sin(A + B)\).

book_ref.quote: multiplying two complex numbers in polar form means multiplying their moduli and adding their arguments

steps: \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2(\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2 + i\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2 + i^{2}\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2)\)
Using \(\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B\) and \(\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B\): \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2[\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2) + i\sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2)]\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved; the product is \(6\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 6i\)

blocks.prompt: 21 Prove that \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}[\cos(\theta_1 - \theta_2) + i\sin(\theta_1 - \theta_2)]\) for \(z_1 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\), \(z_2 = r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2) \ne 0\). Hence divide \(10\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\) by \(5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by \(\cos\theta_2 - i\sin\theta_2\); the denominator becomes 1.

book_ref.quote: the modulus of the result is the quotient of their moduli

blocks.final_answer: Hence proved; the quotient is \(2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2i\)

blocks.prompt: 22 If \(z_1 = 4\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) and \(z_2 = 2\left(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\), find \(z_1 z_2\), \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\) and \(z_1 + z_2\) in the form \(x + iy\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the polar rules for the product and the quotient; for the sum go to rectangular form.

book_ref.quote: There is no shortcut for adding in polar form.

blocks.prompt: 23 If \(z = x + iy\), write the equation \(|2z + i| = |2\overline{z} - 4|\) in terms of \(x\) and \(y\), and name the curve. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write each side as \(a + ib\), take moduli, square and simplify.

book_ref.quote: represents a straight line in the complex plane

blocks.prompt: 24 If \(z = x + iy\) and \(\arg\left(\dfrac{z - 1}{z + 1}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), show that \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the fraction as \(a + ib\) using the conjugate of the denominator; an argument of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) means the real part is 0 and the imaginary part is positive.

book_ref.quote: The exact locus is the part of the circle with

steps: \(\arg = \frac{\pi}{2}\): the number lies on the positive imaginary axis, so the real part is 0 (and \(2y > 0\))

blocks.prompt: 25 A voltage \(V = 50\) volts is applied to a circuit of impedance \(Z = 3 + 4i\) ohms. Find the current in rectangular form and in polar form. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(V = IZ\), so \(I = V/Z\); divide with the conjugate, then find modulus and angle.

book_ref.quote: resistance generalizes to impedance

blocks.prompt: 26 Using A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26, encrypt the word SUM by multiplying by the key \(k = 3 + 2i\), and then decrypt it using the multiplicative inverse of \(k\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Encryption is multiplication by \(k\); decryption is multiplication by \(k^{-1} = \overline{k}/|k|^{2}\).
